score_matrix.rationale: The patch applies cleanly, touches only OPEN_QUESTIONS.md, keeps Status Open with all metadata intact, and updates the Resolution in the existing style while marking the contract as awaiting operator approval, which fits the question's human-approval requirement. The gap it identifies is real on the face of the question text: the handoff repeatedly relies on scoped, friction-only, withdrawn, replaced and competing corrections, yet the minimum repair only names `correction_of` and `annotation_of`, so the required planner, report and reopen fixtures have no defined interpretation to assert against. The proposed contract stays within existing event types and the arbitrary JSON payload, keeps legacy unscoped corrections unrewritten, and routes overlapping competing corrections to ordinary review rather than timestamps, all consistent with D0071 and D0248 as the question describes them. Points are withheld because key premises (D0071 content, `event_payload`/`result`/`effective_at` field names, D0248's class name) are asserted without evidence available in the request and partly contradict the recorded `payload` field name, because path-scoped withdraw is left semantically undefined, and because the proposal grows an already oversized question body with a data-model choice that would be more auditable as a separate approval item.
required_fixes: Cite the UBU-D0071 and DESIGN.md text that establishes correction scope is undefined, or soften the claim to what the question already records (the 2026-10-14 audit found no event-specific validation).

Align `corrected_paths` target field names with the recorded Log envelope (`payload` per the NewLogRecord audit) or cite the DESIGN.md section that defines `event_payload`, `result` and `effective_at`.
Define corrected-view semantics for a path-scoped `withdraw`, or restrict `withdraw` to the whole assertion so every declared scope has deterministic interpretation.
Consider recording the contract as an explicit approval item (candidate decision or dependent question linked under Depends on) rather than only in the minimum-repair prose.
risks: The claim that UBU-D0071 defines only annotation/correction links with optional old/new values is not corroborated by anything in the request; if D0071 or DESIGN.md already defines a scope or kind mechanism, the new contract would conflict with recorded design rather than fill a gap.

The contract names target fields `event_payload`, `result` and `effective_at`, but the recorded audits describe the Log request as `id`, `event_type`, `object_refs`, `payload`, `provenance`, `created_at` (NewLogRecord uses `payload`). Field names in the contract may not match the actual envelope, which would make the `corrected_paths` rules unimplementable as written.

Path-scoped `withdraw` is permitted (`corrected_paths` may be listed for withdraw) but only whole-assertion withdraw has defined corrected-view semantics; path-scoped withdraw is left undefined, which reintroduces the free-form interpretation the contract is meant to remove.
The reference to `UBU-D0248`'s incompatible-intent class asserts specific content of that decision that cannot be verified from the request.

A new data-model contract (`correction_kind`, `corrected_paths`) is embedded in an already very long question body instead of a candidate decision or a dependent question, making the approval item easy to lose and further inflating the question text.
Author did not run git apply --check and estimated hunk line numbers; mechanical validation reports the patch applies, so this is residual only.
